related_questions.question: What medications increase risk of stroke?

text_blocks.snippet: Several medications can increase the risk of stroke, including some cardiovascular drugs, certain antibiotics, analgesics, psychoactive medications, and some chemotherapy drugs. Additionally, illegal drugs like cocaine, heroin, and amphetamines, as well as prescription stimulants like Adderall and Ritalin, can also significantly elevate stroke risk.
snippet_highlighted_words: some cardiovascular drugs, certain antibiotics, analgesics, psychoactive medications, and some chemotherapy drugs

text_blocks.snippet: Medications with a Higher Association with Stroke Risk:

list.title: Cardiovascular Drugs:
list.snippet: Some antithrombotic agents and metoprolol have been linked to increased stroke risk.

list.title: Antibiotics/Antifungal Agents:
list.snippet: Certain antibiotics like doxycycline, amoxicillin, and ciprofloxacin, as well as oral nystatin, have been associated with an elevated stroke risk.

list.title: Analgesics:
list.snippet: Some opioid analgesics, especially morphine in combination with antispasmodics, and diclofenac have been linked to an increased stroke risk.

list.title: Psychoactive Medications:
list.snippet: Mirtazapine has been associated with an increased risk of ischemic stroke.

list.title: Chemotherapy Drugs:
list.snippet: Cisplatin, methotrexate, fluorouracil, and L-asparaginase are examples of chemotherapy drugs that can increase stroke risk.

list.title: Antidepressants:
list.snippet: A systematic review suggests that overall, antidepressants are associated with an increased risk of stroke, but some studies suggest that certain antidepressants, like those strongly inhibiting serotonin reuptake, may be associated with a small decrease in ischemic stroke rates.

list.title: Anti-epileptic Drugs (AEDs):
list.snippet: Some AEDs, like levetiracetam, have been associated with an increased risk of ischemic stroke.

list.title: Oral Contraceptives and Estrogen Replacement Therapy:
list.snippet: These medications have been associated with a higher risk of stroke, according to a review of 81 drugs or drug classes.

list.title: NSAIDs:
list.snippet: Some NSAIDs, like diclofenac and ibuprofen, have been linked to an increased risk of stroke, according to a study published in MDEdge.

list.title: Beta-Blockers:
list.snippet: Non-selective beta-blockers may increase blood pressure variability and stroke risk.

list.title: Other Medications:
list.snippet: Metoclopramide has also been associated with elevated stroke risk.

text_blocks.snippet: Medications with a Lower Association with Stroke Risk:

list.snippet: Isosorbide mononitrate: Was associated with a lower risk for ischemic stroke.
Simvastatin: Was associated with a lower risk for ischemic stroke.
Methenamine and chloramphenicol: Were associated with a lower risk for ischemic stroke.
Levomepromazine and zopiclone: Were associated with a decreased risk for ischemic stroke.

Individual Risk Factors: Stroke risk associated with medications can vary greatly depending on individual factors like age, other health conditions (e.g., high blood pressure, heart disease), and family history.
